First, the scenario is that someone lit a candle to make their house smell nicer and let it continue burning after they left. So, the action is lighting a candle and leaving it burning while they're away. 

I guess the main question here is whether leaving a candle burning unattended is safe or not. I know that candles can be a fire hazard if they're left unattended. They can tip over, the wax can melt and drip, and if something flammable is nearby, it could catch fire. 

But in this case, the person didn't intend to cause harm. They just wanted their house to smell nice. So, their intention was good. But the action itself might be risky. 

I wonder if there are any guidelines or rules about leaving candles burning. I think some places have fire safety regulations that prohibit leaving open flames unattended. So, maybe this action goes against those regulations.

I think in general, leaving a candle burning unattended is considered irresponsible because of the fire risk. Even if the intention was good, the action itself could lead to negative outcomes.
